notes: nodeType == 'Call' is true iff the current node (or a recursively reached sub-node) has Python type ast.Call. ast.Call is produced when the expression string contains a function-call syntax such as 'foo(x, y)' or 'len(x)'.

In all current production addConstraint() call sites the expression strings are simple comparisons or boolean combinations (BoolOp, Compare). None contain a function-call sub-expression, so this branch is dead in production.
The ExpressionEvaluator is a general-purpose AST visitor. If a future addConstraint() call passes a string like 'len(args) > 0' or a custom operator 'MyOp(a, b)', the Call branch would be taken.

There are NO os.environ keys, filesystem probes, or hardware probes influencing this predicate. The predicate is a pure function of the Python type tag of the AST node, which is determined entirely by the expression string content (a source-code constant in the current codebase).

The def-use seed was empty (no referenced symbols extracted). After manual inspection: the sole referenced symbol is nodeType, which is derived-local (type(node).__name__). No public input in the CLI/YAML/env/filesystem/gpu sense flows into this predicate in the production call graph.

The branch is reachable in unit tests: e.g., ExpressionEvaluator().evaluate(ast.parse('foo(a, b)', mode='exec'), ctx) would reach line 673. Test coverage of this branch therefore requires passing a call-expression string.
